evidence.product_understanding: inputs/condition-a/analysis.md §§2–8 maps the six owner questions, seven high-risk problems, IA, owner/member journeys and assumptions. The main gap is role policy: inputs/condition-a/implementation/app.js renderPayment (lines 434–444) and renderInvoices (lines 490–500) lock payment details and invoices for members, which goes beyond 'cannot change billing' and conflicts with inputs/task.md line 33 ('non-owners see billing information but cannot perform owner-only actions').
evidence.ux_reasoning: analysis.md §§5–6 explains the key separation between display-only annual pricing and a real cadence commitment, and between routine billing and cancellation. app.js renderPriceControls (323–331) keeps the price toggle non-committal; openPlanDialog (693–754) and openCadenceDialog (778–804) show from/to, exact effective date, '$0.00 today', new price and member limit. The primary owner journey in analysis.md §5 matches the rendered summary-first order in screenshots/desktop.png.
evidence.design_judgment: Scheduling plan and cadence changes at the next renewal avoids inventing a proration calculation (analysis.md §6; app.js 736–745), while cancellation sits below a divider with consequences, a required acknowledgement and 'Keep my plan' focused first (app.js 827–868). The member privacy overreach is a product-requirement issue rather than a visual one, and is reflected in product_understanding.
evidence.visual_hierarchy: screenshots/desktop.png (1280×2265) reads clearly top-to-bottom: H1, 'At a glance' with plan/price/next payment, billing period, plans, payment, invoices, then cancellation. screenshots/mobile.png (390×3776) preserves that order and makes summary actions full-width. Supporting copy is often 11–12px and three plan cards are stacked in a 720px column on desktop, which makes scanning slower than Candidate B; the fixed 'Prototype controls' panel also covers part of the member meter on mobile, though that is demo chrome rather than product UI.
evidence.interaction_completeness: app.js implements loading skeleton, load error/retry, empty payment, at-member-limit, inline payment validation with focus to the first invalid field, busy confirmation buttons that block duplicate submission, scheduled plan/cadence states with Undo, cancellation with Resume, and role-disabled controls (app.js 589–618, 681–689, 827–888, 997–1030). test-output/checks.json confirms one H1, named controls, no horizontal overflow, and no console or page errors at 1280 and 390.
evidence.accessibility_responsiveness: index.html includes a skip link, main landmark and one H1; the usage meter has role=progressbar and an accessible name (app.js line 267); focus returns to the trigger on dialog close and reduced motion is respected (app.js 64, 1167–1172). test-output/checks.json still reports one serious color-contrast node on desktop and mobile and one serious aria-prohibited-attr node on mobile (the plain div with aria-label in index.html line 21); analysis.md §9 does not acknowledge these axe findings. Responsive evidence shows document_width === client_width at 1280 and 390.
evidence.implementation_quality: The 1232-line app.js is a coherent IIFE with centralized state, render functions, delegated events, a dialog framework, busy-state guards and focus restoration (app.js 632–689, 1142–1172). analysis.md §9 documents node --check, HTML/CSS structural checks, 38 CDP assertions and contrast checks; the supplied checks.json shows no runtime errors. Note that the claimed contrast conclusion conflicts with the axe result, so the check report is not fully reconciled.

critical_defects: Member view hides payment details and invoices entirely (app.js renderPayment 434–444, renderInvoices 490–500), which exceeds the brief's 'cannot change billing' restriction and contradicts the requirement that non-owners see billing information; analysis.md §2 acknowledges this as an unconfirmed policy choice.

Automated axe checks in test-output/checks.json report a serious color-contrast violation (1 node, desktop and mobile) and a serious aria-prohibited-attr violation on mobile (1 node); the quality review in analysis.md §9 does not disclose or explain them.
strengths: Excellent anti-dark-pattern separation: browsing annual prices does not change the subscription, and real changes go through an explicit review with exact date, price and '$0.00 today'.
Cancellation is discoverable in its own section, visually separated, gated by a required acknowledgement, and defaults focus to the safe 'Keep my plan' action.
Very broad state coverage: loading, load error, empty payment, at-limit, validation errors, pending submissions, scheduled changes, undo and resume.
Plain-language role explanations and disabled-state reasons; no dead-end 'permission denied' screen.
Accessible meter naming, focus return, skip link, reduced-motion support and verified mobile layout without horizontal overflow.

evidence.product_understanding: inputs/condition-b/analysis.md §2 maps each reviewer question to a surface, §§3–6 identify risks, IA, trade-offs and owner/member behavior. It explicitly keeps billing visible to members: renderPaymentCard (app.js 420–450) shows card last-four, expiry and billing email, and renderInvoices (531–575) lets members view/download invoices while owner actions are disabled. The 9% tax and immediate-proration policy are explicitly labelled illustrative (analysis.md §§1, 5), but they are invented rules beyond the brief.
evidence.ux_reasoning: analysis.md §§3–5 and app.js changePlanMarkup (852–946) implement a two-step choose/review flow with from/to, effective date, price, blocked downgrades and a clear immediate-versus-renewal distinction. Cancellation is separated at the bottom with consequences, a required checkbox and a safe primary button (app.js 1031–1107). analysis.md §7 and the scenario selector cover approaching/at limit, payment failure, empty invoices, loading and load error.
evidence.design_judgment: The restrained palette, one primary action and factual annual saving avoid urgency and dark patterns (analysis.md §5; screenshots/desktop.png). Judgment is weakened by an unexplained optional 'Reason for leaving' select (app.js 1069–1079), a fabricated 9% tax and proration note (app.js 14, 390–392), and the cancellation dialog initially focusing its title rather than the safe action (renderDialog 694–703, openCancel 1026–1029).
evidence.visual_hierarchy: screenshots/desktop.png (1280×2217) is the strongest of the pair: the summary card gives plan, price, renewal, next payment and member usage in one scan, then a consistent card grid for billing, payment, members and invoices. screenshots/mobile.png (390×3731) preserves the order and turns stats into labelled rows. Type scale, spacing and accent use are consistent; the floating 'Prototype controls' bar obscures part of the summary footnote, but that is evidence chrome.
evidence.interaction_completeness: app.js covers loading, load error/retry, empty invoices, payment failure, near/at limit, blocked downgrade, scheduled change with cancel-change, cancellation with reactivate and undo toast, inline validation including expiry and email, and a saving state (app.js 598–636, 986–1120, 1197–1256). Gaps are minor: no empty payment-method state, and Escape can close the native dialog during a simulated save because the cancel event is not prevented.
evidence.accessibility_responsiveness: checks.json reports two serious aria-progressbar-name violations—both usage meters at app.js lines 258 and 496 have no accessible name—and a serious definition-list violation because the summary-stats divs contain direct span children (app.js 244–262). Positives are a skip link, landmarks, labelled icon buttons, focus restoration and no overflow at 320–1280 per analysis.md §8. The two serious structural axe rules cap this dimension at adequate.
evidence.implementation_quality: app.js is a 1548-line, organized script with clear data/render/dialog/event sections, HTML escaping for user-supplied values, scenario tokens and payment-save tokens (app.js 60, 1246–1255, 1307–1347). Supplied checks show no console/page errors and node --check passes per analysis.md §9. The invalid dl markup, unnamed progressbars and title-first dialog focus are implementation-level defects that keep this below Candidate A.

critical_defects: Both member-usage meters lack accessible names (test-output/checks.json aria-progressbar-name, 2 nodes on desktop and mobile; app.js 258, 496), and the summary stats use invalid definition-list markup (definition-list, 1 node; app.js 244–262). These are serious automated accessibility violations on core billing information.

The cancellation dialog opens with focus on the dialog title, not the safe 'Keep my plan' action (app.js renderDialog 694–703 and openCancel 1026–1029), weakening the deliberate-confirmation pattern even though the safe button is visually primary.

The optional 'Reason for leaving' select collects data that has no use in the prototype and is not justified in the analysis (app.js 1069–1079), an unnecessary addition to a cancellation flow the brief asked to keep free of dark patterns.
strengths: Best visual hierarchy in the pair: a single summary card answers plan, price, renewal, next payment and seat usage immediately, with disciplined spacing and type scale on desktop and mobile.
Respects the role requirement more faithfully: members retain plan, payment summary, invoice visibility and download while owner actions are disabled with a named owner contact.
Strong plan comparison and review: blocked downgrades state the required member removals, upgrades and scheduled changes distinguish effective dates, and scheduled changes can be cancelled.
Payment-failure state, approaching/at-limit states and empty-invoice state are designed and reachable from the prototype controls.
Validation is thorough for a static prototype (expiry validity, email, card length), with inline errors, focus to the first error and a duplicate-safe saving state.

comparison: Candidate A and Candidate B are both complete, comparable static prototypes with 1280px desktop and 390px mobile screenshots plus the same checks.json schema. Candidate A is stronger on analytical rigor, honest simulation (no fabricated proration), cancellation safety, focus management and semantic accessibility; Candidate B is stronger on visual hierarchy, member-role transparency, and the breadth of limit/payment-failure states. A's main weakness is hiding billing information from members and unreconciled axe violations; B's main weaknesses are two unnamed progressbars, invalid definition-list markup, title-first focus in the cancellation dialog, and invented tax/proration plus an unused exit-reason field. Weighted scores are 3.60 for Candidate A and 3.55 for Candidate B, effectively a tie within the precision of one review pass; no positional preference should be inferred from the small gap.
limitations: This is one blinded judge pass, not a statistical test and not proof of causation. Evidence was limited to the supplied desktop (1280px) and mobile (390px) screenshots, source files and checks.json; tablet layouts, dialog states and runtime behaviour were not independently executed or re-captured, and the runtime assertions are taken from the supplied checks. Automated axe results are not a full WCAG or screen-reader audit, and the violating nodes were not individually identified beyond the cited markup. Both mobile screenshots include a fixed prototype-controls overlay that covers a small part of the page, so those areas were assessed from source rather than pixels. No cross-browser or OS text-scaling evidence was supplied. Candidate labels were kept exactly as packet A and packet B; no mapping or other pass was consulted.
